chapter: Cotton Club, Zutty and Chicago traditions
title: Bill Johnson, Pops Foster and the New Orleans routes to Chicago and San Francisco
summary: Hinton explains the river and sea migration of New Orleans musicians and Taylor remembers Pops Foster's late years.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Yeah, that‟s right too. It was great to see, and I can see myself and knowing… hearing Bill Johnson, this great bass player that was so strong. I didn‟t see Pops Foster. You see, if you knew all those people, they had two routes, they followed the ocean or the water or people followed the river of New Orleans right up the Mississippi River, came on up to St Louis and then into Chicago. The other group came from New Orleans and followed the sea and went right on to San Francisco. A great group of New Orleans people in San Francisco but they were people from [Unintelligible] Stevedore part and people that followed… Pop Foster even went there and died out that way years later.

Right, yeah. I met him… I had met him in New York but I really got to know him fairly well in these last years when he was playing with Earl Hines and he was doing some things out in San Francisco. He was a wonderful old man.
I mean he was very old when I met him but man he was playing, he could play [laugh].
He sure was and he was so concerned with young people.
